speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing dizziness, nausea, and imbalance; could you please describe exactly when these symptoms started and if they feel like the room is spinning or more like general lightheadedness? To help me assess this quickly, have you noticed any hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or recent head trauma?

speaker: Patient
text: 27-year-old male. The patient reports a sustained sensation of the room spinning since this morning, which is low grade and constant. He occasionally feels nauseous and has taken diphenhydramine to help him sleep, which also alleviates his symptoms slightly. He mentions recent increased intake of garlic due to trying to recover from a cold a few days ago. Past medical history is unremarkable.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV) is unlikely given the constant nature; the clinical picture of sustained vertigo with nausea and no hearing loss in a young male is most consistent with Vestibular Neuritis or potentially a viral labyrinthitis without auditory involvement. Given the lack of hearing loss and the specific mention of "spinning," I am considering a viral etiology affecting the vestibular nerve.
